subQuests.subQuestName: Wait for the debate two days later (15:00 – 18:00)

130080101.text: Hello and welcome, everyone. I am Safwan, a scholar from the Akademiya, and I will serve as this debate's adjudicator.

130080102.text: I swear to judge both parties with the utmost wisdom and impartiality. I will neither interfere with the proceedings nor demonstrate bias.

130080103.text: I ask for both parties to stand. May the Dendro Archon also serve as a witness to this duel of wits.

130080104.text: Since you so desperately demand an explanation, I will expound on the Akademiya's stance.

130080105.text: You may have misunderstood us from the outset, and believed that the Akademiya is prejudiced against you.

130080106.text: However, the truth is that the Akademiya wishes for every resident of Sumeru to be afforded opportunities to grow and cultivate their wisdom.

130080107.text: Therefore, the works they consume should also possess enlightening qualities and intellectual value.

130080108.text: We have failed to identify these qualities in the shows performed at Zubayr Theater.

130080109.text: In other words, instead of struggling against the Akademiya in pointless confrontations, if you had spent your time reflecting on improving the quality of your shows and enlightening your audience...

130080110.text: Zubayr Theater would not be today facing such a tragic fate.

130080111.text: Aggressive from the get-go. He's really putting on the pressure...!

130080113.text: (Calm down, Nilou... First, carefully analyze what he said.)

130080114.text: (He said that we were shut down not because the Akademiya looks down on the arts, but rather because our shows aren't up to their standards. However...)

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the theater and witness the debate

130080213.text: (She already agreed to this. She wants to win, no matter what. Me too.)

130080214.text: Mr. Sharif believes that interpersonal relationships are a byproduct of working towards a goal. Once that goal is achieved or abandoned, those relationships would have no more reason to continue.

130080215.text: Then, if someone has failed to live up to his expectations—

130080216.text: If someone has failed to live up to your expectations and ran away from home, then she shouldn't be your daughter anymore, right?

130080218.text: Sorry Nilou, as expected, I should be the one to say it. You don't need to shoulder this responsibility for me.

130080220.text: If in your eyes, the purpose of my existence is to become your academic successor, then that goal has ended in complete failure.

130080221.text: By your logic, that means there is no more reason to sustain our relationship as father and daughter.

130080222.text: Members of the audience who do not belong to either debate party, please speak with caution.

130080224.text: What she does not say, Nilou will.

130080225.text: No matter how many disagreements we've had, the truth is that you are still my father.

130080226.text: You're so immersed in your own world that you can't understand why we come together for the sake of relationships.

130080227.text: Yeah, don't look down on us!

130080228.text: You can watch a dance anywhere, but there's only one Zubayr Theater!

130080229.text: I'm almost starting to feel sorry for this guy, what with the idiotic things he's said.

130080230.text: Order, order! Members of the audience, do not interrupt debate proceedings!

130080231.text: I confess that this is the final argument we had prepared. Disown me, and you will win the debate.

130080232.text: But before that, Father, I have some final words to say.

130080233.text: I've been doing some soul-searching. Not about whether I should have run away from home, but whether there was any point to my personal rebellion against you.

130080234.text: I kept trying to earn your approval, but I only disappointed you over and over. The truth is, I ran away from home as a means to vent my recurring frustrations.

130080235.text: That is to say, I was exerting pressure on you, and hoping you'd give up on your lofty expectations.

130080236.text: But by doing that, wasn't I just doing the same thing as you?

130080238.text: I won't force my expectations upon you anymore. At Zubayr Theater, I have found the life I've always wanted.

130080239.text: I will move on from my family troubles and strive towards my new goal.

130080240.text: But if you dare to harm this place, then I will stand with my friends here and fight against you.

130080241.text: This is not the time to space out, Sharif. The debate is still underway.

130080242.text: ...You already consider them to be your friends?

130080243.text: You should be asking US that question.

130080245.text: Miss Inayah is a really good friend!

130080246.text: It was a bit of a process, but we won her over.

130080248.text: All those who come to Zubayr Theater become one of us. We will always be with her.

130080251.text: Wait, what are you...? Ah, never mind.

130080259.text: I relaxed for a moment, and... I feel a little faint...

130080260.text: It looks like he still has a place for her in his heart.

130080261.text: Terrific work, Nilou and Inayah. They likely won't cause any more trouble for us.

130080262.text: Didn't know you could get so fierce. I have a lot of newfound respect for you two.

130080263.text: This really took a lot out of me, though. *sigh* I don't ever wanna do this again...

130080264.text: Both Miss Nilou and Miss Inayah were so cool!

130080265.text: Should we throw a second round of celebrations?

130080266.text: The curtain finally falls on the debate amidst a euphony of cheers...

130080403.text: Yes, I feel a lot better. The more I think back on everything, the more surreal it all feels.

130080404.text: I don't think I could repeat what I did a second time.

130080405.text: All of our preparations paid off.

130080406.text: Yes, and it's all thanks to you.

130080409.text: Hehe, I see. You mean how fate brought me to the theater, right?

130080410.text: Then, I'll have to tell you about my teacher, who Mr. Zubayr had mentioned.

130080411.text: Mr. Zubayr opened his theater when I was still a child.

130080412.text: There was a beautiful dancer, and from the moment I saw her, I couldn't look away.

130080413.text: I thought to myself, "The gods must have blessed her with such talent."

130080414.text: But later on, she would actually smile down at me and say, "Just the opposite, in fact."

130080416.text: Yeah. She said, "Dance is an art born from toil. It isn't a gift from the gods, but a creation by our own hands."

130080417.text: "It is a beautiful thing born from our life experiences. Whenever there is joy or something to be celebrated, people will dance."

130080418.text: "In other words, any place where people can effortlessly begin a dance will for sure be filled with the blessings of everyone's happiness."

130080419.text: She wasn't looking for flowers and applause — all she wanted was to see her audience smile.

130080601.text: Everyone, I'd like to introduce you to our newest member: Inayah!

130080603.text: She'll be dancing for us from now on, so please give her your support.

130080604.text: Inayah's taken her place on the stage! Paimon wonders how she'll look once she starts dancing.

130080605.text: When you stop and think about it, happy endings like this sure aren't easy to come by!

130080606.text: A lot of things came together to make it happen.

130080607.text: Nilou's efforts, everyone's wisdom, Inayah's determination...

130080609.text: Huh? What do you mean by that?

130080612.text: You do have a point there...

130080613.text: The whole demolition thing was going overboard, but he really could've banned Nilou and the others from dancing.

130080614.text: If he really wanted to be ruthless, he could've done some real damage, even without winning the debate.

130080615.text: Oh well, it's not like we can understand how people like him think. Let's focus on watching the performance!

subQuests.subQuestName: Go to the theater to see Inayah

130080501.text: You two are welcome here anytime! Seeing you safe and sound in between adventures will keep me from worrying too much about you.

130080502.text: I think I already see you two as people of the Grand Bazaar. Yep, without a doubt.

130080301.text: During the debate, you said that you found a new wish. What was it?

130080302.text: I actually... want to learn how to dance from Nilou.

130080303.text: That's a great wish, but with your shyness, are you really going to be okay going up on stage?

130080305.text: Nilou wasn't born an expert, either!

130062901.text: Due to special circumstances, all theatrical performances have been cancelled and the resumption time has yet to be determined. Sorry about the inconvenience.

130071701.text: Everything is ready. The only thing left is to wait until the day after tomorrow.

130071702.text: Hehe, I hope I'll actually be able to get some sleep over the next two nights.

130080118.text: In your eyes, our shows can't meet the Akademiya's expectations.

130080119.text: Shouldn't it be the audience who decides if a show is intellectual or enlightening? Why is someone from the Akademiya judging that?

130080120.text: Also, I believe that there is no such thing as a wiser or more enlightening performance.

130080121.text: Art doesn't discriminate, and it appeals to all. Everyone has the right to appreciate art.

130080122.text: Appreciation is but a primitive form of satisfaction. Guidance and enlightenment are necessary if we are to induce growth in the performers as well as the audience.

130080123.text: This stance holds performers to a higher standard and encourages the development of the arts.

130080124.text: If all performances are simple-minded, require little effort to comprehend, and lack any impetus for the betterment of society, then the people will not be able to develop a greater level of artistic understanding.

130080125.text: Nurturing the populace's understanding requires a long and arduous process, and guiding this process is the Akademiya's true goal.

130080126.text: (He changed the topic without batting an eye! Good thing I'm prepared.)

130080127.text: (If I remember correctly, what I should say here is...)

130080131.text: Someone at our theater has tried that before.

130080132.text: He was a famed artist, but he recognized that very few people could connect with his works.

130080133.text: I agree that art should be enlightening, but we can't pursue that goal by creating complicated works.

130080134.text: If a work can't tap into an audience's personal experiences or feelings, then its contents may as well be a castle in the sky.

130080135.text: What's the point of performing a show that its audience can't even follow?

130080136.text: That would only be forcing people to watch something they don't like.

130080137.text: You can only reach that conclusion from a place of ignorance.

130080138.text: In that case, before passing judgment, you should first become a better dancer than me.

130080140.text: Looks like he's backed himself into a corner...

130080141.text: As the party holding the burden of proof, Sharif has failed to provide sufficient support for his judgment of the quality of Zubayr Theater's programs.

130080142.text: Likewise, the definition that Nilou put forth is but her personal opinion. Neither party is the victor for this particular point of contention.

130080143.text: ...Additionally, I must request that both parties exercise greater control on their emotions.

130080144.text: Keep it up, Nilou! You're doing great!

130080145.text: In that case, I shall speak of more concrete matters. The essence of this issue is that you have violated the law, so you must now pay the price for your transgression.

130080146.text: This course of action is also completely procedurally sound. We have already contacted Zubayr Theater multiple times regarding the theater's repertoire.

130080147.text: However, you have consciously ignored our warnings — or perhaps your compliance was purely superficial. Regardless, that failure has indirectly led to the present day's proceedings.

130080148.text: That is indeed so, according to the laws decreed by the Akademiya.

130080149.text: (He's started talking about procedural stuff, so I need to focus on...)

130080153.text: Mr. Zubayr has already provided signed copies of all documentation related to our operations. Everything is perfectly filled out and valid.

130080154.text: Although the theater's performances don't align with the Akademiya's requests, the law doesn't say that Zubayr Theater can be demolished only because of that reason.

130080155.text: Demolition notices need to be provided in writing and made available to the public. Otherwise, the theater can continue to operate as long as its license is valid.

130080156.text: Failing to follow these rules makes your stance procedurally unsound.

130080159.text: ...There are different ways to apply the rules. There is precedent for this.

130080160.text: So long as this matter is discussed within the Akademiya, this course of action will come to pass.

130080161.text: Looking at the past 27 cases of similar nature, 90% of them support Sharif's claim and position.

130080162.text: However, the demolition process in those cases was only started after discussion at the Akademiya. In other words, premature notice of demolition is indeed a rash act.

130080163.text: That's more than enough. We've proven that the order is unreasonable as it currently stands.

130080165.text: Nilou's definitely won this point, right?

130080169.text: Even if permission for demolition has yet to be obtained, it is a fact that your performances violated the Akademiya's policies on numerous occasions.

130080170.text: Based on that fact, we can permanently revoke your right to perform in Sumeru.

130080172.text: Under the current system, it is indeed possible to immediately revoke Zubayr Theater's performing rights.

130080188.text: Zubayr Theater isn't simply a performance venue to us — it means more than that. It's been our home for a long time.

130080189.text: Ms. Rekhar can't go on adventures anymore, but she has found a stable career and a new life at the theater.

130080190.text: Her son, Sohrin, has already passed his theater exam, and he'll soon be our newest member.

130080191.text: Mr. Khasani found a new way to look at art. He decided to stay at the theater to watch us grow.

130080192.text: Mr. Farhad and Mr. Hushang visit even when there isn't a show going on, and they always tell us lots of entertaining stories.

130080193.text: Even Inayah wants to stay with us, and she's starting to look forward to a new future.

130080194.text: Zubayr Theater exists for them... for every single one of us!

130080195.text: Perhaps Zubayr Theater has provided you with a multitude of positive emotions and experiences. However, you have misconstrued something, young miss.

130080196.text: The interpersonal relationships you speak of were established upon normal theater operations.

130080197.text: Sheikh Zubayr operates the theater for his livelihood, his employees work for their wages, and the audience comes to enjoy performances.

130080198.text: Relationships are merely a byproduct in this exchange of interests. They may be pleasant and captivating, but they can only ever be secondary.

130080199.text: When scholars collaborate to solve difficult problems, we freely share our knowledge and resources with one another, as if we were all kin.

130080200.text: However, this collaboration ends after the results of our work are published.

130080201.text: The reason is simple: We are scholars, and there are new projects that await our attention.

130080202.text: He really doesn't think much of relationships. Paimon also thinks he did a lot of prep — he's been solid as a rock.

130080203.text: Sharif's argument is currently the more persuasive of the two for this point of contention.

130080204.text: The continuance of the interpersonal relationships Nilou spoke of remains hypothetical before the theater's demolition, whereas the situation that Sharif described has been well documented at the Akademiya.

130080205.text: The Akademiya has made significant academic contributions in no small part due to its researchers' efficiency and ability to compartmentalize.

130080206.text: Oh no, what should we do? Things are going in the opposite direction...

130080209.text: A set-up? So Nilou's got him?

130080210.text: (Good, he's said what he said. The next argument could decide this debate.)

130080211.text: (But... is this really the best thing to do? It might be too cruel to Inayah...)

130089901.text: In the blink of an eye, it's already debate time!

130089902.text: We did a lot of preparations with Nilou! Hopefully they were helpful.

130089903.text: Are you still worried about Inayah?

130089904.text: Let's be sure to come back often. Who knows, maybe things will have worked out for her!

130089905.text: (Don't think that would make for a good rebuttal.)

130089907.text: (I need to rethink things. This is a crucial moment, so I can't mess up.)

130089909.text: (I can't seem to make a connection here.)

130089910.text: The most important thing about an experience is how you choose to interpret it.

130089911.text: Art must first be appreciated by others to confer value.

130089912.text: (Mr. Zubayr has been meticulously managing the theater. Everything checks out.)

130089913.text: (Everyone is free to appreciate art — no form of art is inherently superior.)

130089914.text: (Inayah really wants to win. She doesn't wanna lose anything else because of her painful past.)

130089915.text: (The theater carries everyone's feelings, and serves as the bond that connects us all.)
